Hi Alex — thanks for the note and for laying out the checklist. We'll get you a consolidated SIG response with artifacts. Quick overview so you know what to expect:

- RTO/RPO: Our standard hosted model ("core") targets RTO <= 30 minutes for control-plane failover and RPO <= 1 hour for customer data restores. For dedicated/reserved deployments we offer configurable RTOs down to 15 minutes (by agreement) and RPOs down to 15 minutes depending on replication policies.
- Backups: Automated incremental backups every 15 minutes (customer KV + metadata), daily full snapshots retained for 30 days by default; longer retention available for Dedicated/Private under contract.
- Regional failover: We have automated cross-region failover for control plane via active/passive routing + DNS failover with health checks plus documented runbook for full stateful failover. Some state reconciliation is manual for edge-cases — we'll flag those in the SIG.
- Evidence: I'll attach the DR runbook, the backup topology diagram, and the last DR exercise log (11/15).

I'll coordinate with Neha and Marissa to populate the SIG spreadsheet and return a completed set of answers by EOD Friday. If procurement wants, we can redact any sensitive operational IPs from attachments.

Regards,

Karthik / team — I'm pulling the runbook and test logs. A couple of internal clarifications before we finalize the SIG answers:

1) For the RTO phrasing, Procurement sometimes expects service-level buckets. I'll propose we list three tiers: Hosted-Standard (RTO 30m / RPO 1h), Hosted-Priority (RTO 15m / RPO 15m on cached assets), Dedicated (configurable to 15m/15m). Approve?

2) The incremental backup cadence: our platform writes KV deltas every 15 minutes; we capture WAL segments continuously and roll up to object storage every 2 hours. Procurement will likely ask about encryption-at-rest keys and KMS rotation policy — Neha, can you confirm the KMS rotation interval so we can cite it?

3) Failover steps: The automated failover covers API control-plane routing and ephemeral compute rehydration. Full customer data rehydration for long-running in-progress sessions requires a manual 'state replay' step documented in the runbook. We'll include the exact step reference (Section 4.2).

Attachments I'm preparing: redwood_dr_runbook_v1.3.pdf (redact internal hostnames), backup_topology_2026-11.png, disaster_recovery_test_log_20261115.csv.

Alex — attaching the completed SIG responses and the supporting artifacts you requested. Summary highlights are below and the full answers are in the attached SIG spreadsheet. If procurement needs any redlines or an abbreviated one-page summary, say the word and we'll produce it.

Summary: 
- RTO/RPO by tier: Hosted-Standard (RTO <= 30 minutes / RPO <= 1 hour); Hosted-Priority (RTO <= 15 minutes / RPO <= 15 minutes for cached/ephemeral customer state); Dedicated (negotiable to 15/15 with reserved replication).
- Backups & retention: Incremental backups (delta writes) every 15 minutes; continuous WAL capture with object-store rollups every 2 hours; daily full snapshots retained 30 days. Backups are encrypted at rest using KMS with annual key rotation.
- Multi-region failover: Automated cross-region detection and DNS failover for control-plane; compute rebuilds use immutable images and state rehydration from recent snapshots. Manual state-replay step (runbook Section 4.2) required for long-running session reconciliation.
- DR test evidence: last DR drill executed 2026-11-15 (4-hour window). Test log attached demonstrating failover initiation, data restoration, and verification steps.

Attachments (redacted where appropriate): redwood_dr_runbook_v1.3.pdf; backup_topology_2026-11.png; disaster_recovery_test_log_20261115.csv

Related artifacts / links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DR-Runbook-Redwood; Jira SEC-724 contains the post-test action items.
